description: Support any agent runtime that speaks the XRoads Agent Protocol (XAP) — not just Claude/Gemini/Codex CLI. Custom agents via HTTP webhooks, stdin/stdout protocol, Python scripts, Docker containers, or any executable. Paperclip is 'agent-agnostic' but has no code awareness. XRoads is agent-agnostic AND code-aware — every custom agent gets the same deep git/PRD/worktree integration.
goals: Universal agent protocol (XAP) that any runtime can implement
Support: CLI processes, HTTP webhooks, stdin/stdout, Docker, Python scripts
Same code-aware context injection for ALL agent types
non_goals: No remote agent execution (agents run locally or via user's own infra)
No agent training/fine-tuning — XRoads orchestrates, not trains

AgentRuntime.description: A registered agent runtime — defines how to communicate with an agent

fields.name: String UNIQUE — display name (e.g. 'Claude Code', 'My Python Agent')
fields.runtimeType: RuntimeType enum — cli, http, stdio, docker, script
fields.command: String? — CLI: executable path, Script: interpreter + path
fields.healthCheckCommand: String? — command to verify agent is operational
fields.configSchema: String? — JSON Schema for agent-specific config
fields.configDefaults: String? — JSON defaults for agent config

protocol_spec.name: XRoads Agent Protocol (XAP)
protocol_spec.description: Lightweight protocol for agent-orchestrator communication. All runtimes must implement these 5 methods.

transport.cli: Stdin/stdout JSON-RPC (one JSON line per message)
transport.http: POST to agent URL with JSON body, JSON response
transport.stdio: Same as CLI but for non-CLI executables
transport.script: Execute script with environment variables, read stdout JSON

user_stories.title: AgentRuntime entity + DB migration + built-in runtimes
user_stories.description: Migration v13: agent_runtime table. Register 3 built-in runtimes on startup: 1) 'Claude Code' (cli, command=nexus-loop, capabilities=[code_edit, test_run, git_ops, file_read, terminal, mcp_tools]). 2) 'Gemini CLI' (cli, command=gemini-loop, capabilities=[code_edit, test_run, file_read]). 3) 'Codex CLI' (cli, command=codex-loop, capabilities=[code_edit, test_run, file_read]). CRUD repo. AgentSlot gains optional 'runtimeId' FK (nullable for backward compat, defaults to built-in based on agentType). Existing agentType field preserved for display.

user_stories.title: XAP transport layer
user_stories.description: Implement XAP communication for each transport type: 1) CLI transport: spawn process, communicate via stdin/stdout JSON lines (reuse ProcessRunner). 2) HTTP transport: async HTTP client (reqwest), POST JSON to agent URL, parse response. 3) stdio transport: spawn executable, pipe JSON through stdin/stdout (similar to CLI but without loop script wrapper). 4) Docker transport: docker run with --rm, pipe via stdin/stdout. 5) Script transport: execute with environment vars (XROADS_SESSION_ID, XROADS_SLOT_INDEX, XROADS_WORKTREE, XROADS_PRD, XROADS_STORY_ID), parse stdout JSON. Each transport implements trait XapTransport with methods: initialize, execute_story, heartbeat, abort, handoff. Timeout handling per transport (configurable, default 30s for heartbeat, 600s for execute_story).
tests: HTTP transport posts and parses response
Docker transport runs container and communicates

user_stories.title: Universal agent spawner
user_stories.description: Upgrade agent_lifecycle.rs spawn_agent to use AgentRuntime. Flow: 1) Resolve runtime from slot's runtimeId (or infer from agentType for backward compat). 2) Generate AGENT.md context (same as before — all agents get code-aware context). 3) Call xap.initialize via appropriate transport. 4) If runtime supports 'terminal' capability, wire PTY output to event bus. 5) If runtime is HTTP, start heartbeat polling loop. 6) Track agent in lifecycle manager with transport reference. Backward compatible — existing claude/gemini/codex slots continue to work via built-in runtimes.
tests: all agents receive same AGENT.md context

user_stories.title: Custom agent registration UI
user_stories.description: Settings panel section for managing agent runtimes: 1) List of registered runtimes (built-in + custom) with enable/disable toggle. 2) 'Add Agent' dialog: name, type selector (CLI/HTTP/Docker/Script), command/URL/image input, capability checkboxes, icon picker, color picker. 3) Health check button — runs healthCheckCommand and shows result. 4) Config editor — JSON editor for agent-specific config using configSchema. 5) Import/export runtimes as JSON (for sharing). 6) Agent appears in slot config dialog's agent type selector alongside built-in types.
tests: health check runs and shows result
custom agent appears in slot config

user_stories.title: Agent adapter SDK scaffold
user_stories.description: Create a minimal SDK/template for building custom XAP-compatible agents. 1) Python template: xroads_agent.py with XapAgent base class, method stubs for all 5 XAP methods, example implementation. 2) Node.js template: xroads-agent.js with same structure. 3) Shell template: xroads-agent.sh with environment variable parsing and JSON output. 4) Each template includes: README with protocol docs, example PRD, test harness that simulates XRoads calls. Templates bundled in app resources and copyable via 'Create Agent Template' button. This makes it trivially easy for anyone to create a custom XRoads agent.
tests: Python template runs and responds to all 5 XAP methods
Shell template parses env vars and outputs JSON
template copy creates files in target dir

user_stories.title: Runtime capability negotiation
user_stories.description: When assigning a runtime to a role/slot, validate that runtime capabilities match role requirements. Role 'backend_engineer' needs: [code_edit, test_run, git_ops]. If assigned runtime only has [code_edit], show warning and list missing capabilities. Orchestration engine uses capabilities to decide: which stories a runtime can handle, whether to skip test-related stories for non-test-capable agents, whether to require a review pass by a review-capable agent. Capability matrix visible in org chart (green check / red X per capability per role).
tests: orchestration skips stories for incapable agents
capability matrix renders in org chart
